# Martinique Secures Studies Grant for €77.5m Marina Expansion Proposal

By Stephen Yardley  ·  Edited by Stephen Yardley

Oct. 22, 2026 [Projects](/news/?category=projects)

Image:  [CACEM / DMS via Marina World](https://www.marinaworld.com/news/afd-cacem-etang-zabricot-marina-expansion-martinique)

AFD will grant €200,000 for environmental studies on a proposed €77.5m expansion of Fort-de-France's Étang Z'Abricot marina from about 500 to nearly 1,100 berths.

## Environmental studies secure funding

The French Development Agency and the Centre Martinique intercommunal authority CACEM have agreed to finance the environmental studies required for a proposed major expansion of Étang Z’Abricot marina in Fort-de-France. The agreement was signed on 6 October 2026 and reported in the marine infrastructure press on 16 October. It represents a planning-stage funding commitment, not approval to begin the full construction project.

AFD is providing a €200,000 grant through its Overseas Fund for impact assessments and documents needed for subsequent regulatory review. Those studies are a necessary step for a waterfront development in a sensitive coastal environment. They should not be confused with the much larger budget required for the marina works themselves, and neither the construction contract nor a commissioning date has been confirmed in the announcement.

# Le Marin Marina

Located in the south of Martinique, the Marina du Marin is the largest marina in the Caribbean. Built in 1985, it offers 830 berths, around a hundred mooring buoys, and a wide range of services. Now a small town of its own, it has grown with shops, a technical area, and numerous nautical activities.

### Commune

[Le Marin](/en/life-in-martinique/communes/le-marin)

### Activities on site or nearby / Awards

## Breadcrumb

Le Marin Marina is now the largest nautical base in the Caribbean and the leading hub for tourist boat rentals, thanks to its fleet of 220 vessels, the character of the site, and the quality of its services. It embodies sailing and boating in all their diversity.

The marina currently offers 750 berths and 100 mooring buoys—an increase of 110 berths and 30 buoys since the creation of the “second basin,” the port’s major expansion.

Located in an ideal sailing zone with more than 50,000 boats—sailboats, motorboats, day‑rental craft, cabin‑charter vessels, and MegaYachts over 24 meters—circulating throughout the Lesser Antilles, recreational boating grew rapidly in the 1980s.

Martinique became a strategic stopover for sailors heading south toward the Windward Islands or north through the Caribbean. Le Marin offered a direct link to Saint Lucia and the Caribbean Sea to the east. The first phase of the port’s development began in the mid‑1980s with the Departmental Nautical Plan, which recognized the site’s potential and its importance for regional development.

# Port de Plaisance du Marin

## Overview

The Marin Yacht Harbor is a Harbor of superlatives. In constant growth since its creation in the early 1990s, it has now become one of the largest Harbors of the lesser Antilles, with a welcoming capacity of 830 berths and 300 mooring-buoys. It can accommodate superyachts up to 50 meters LOA with a 4.80-meter draft and has the highest flow rate at the pump of the Caribbean (10m3/hour), in terms of fuel bunkering.

### Facilities include:

The Harbor Office as well as the Fuel Station are open every day. The Port de Plaisance du Marin is a French Oasis with all European standards, where luxury motor and sailing yachts will have access to high-quality service repairs, while crews and owners will be able to enjoy the French Caribbean way of life and warm welcome.
